answer: Because the quill count is verified against the nadir text itself, the voyage audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 5 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. Filling 119 aliases hence means producing 119 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. That is 37 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
